boards.title: What the Campus Tour Skips: 10 Places Students Share With Each Other
boards.description: Ten named University of Portland spaces for studying, gathering, reflection, recreation, and campus events.

cards.title: Settle into Franz Lounge
cards.subtitle: Dundon-Berchtold Hall
cards.notes: Bring a reading or laptop to the lounge’s armchairs and tables, then move to another common area if a scheduled event needs the room.
cards.short_summary: A furnished Dundon-Berchtold Hall lounge suited to individual work between classes.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies Franz Lounge in Dundon-Berchtold Hall as a spacious study option with settees, coffee tables, and armchairs.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Dundon-Berchtold Hall; follow posted room-use guidance.

cards.title: Use Clark Library’s study choices
cards.subtitle: Clark Library
cards.notes: Choose the seating that fits your task, or reserve a group room, booth, or individual carrel through the library’s current process.
cards.short_summary: The campus library combines quiet seating with reservable study spaces.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland says Clark Library offers quiet study, seating and outlets, plus reservable group study rooms, booths, and individual carrels.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Library spaces and room reservations may have current eligibility or booking rules.

cards.title: Work by the Vollum Study Room windows
cards.subtitle: Shiley Hall
cards.notes: Use a desk or reference shelf in this two-floor study space, and keep the room ready for others by packing out your materials when finished.
cards.short_summary: A two-level School of Engineering study room with desks, reference materials, and windows.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the Vollum Study Room in Shiley Hall as a two-floor space with desks, reference materials, and a wall of windows.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in Shiley Hall; observe any school or room-use notices.

cards.title: Read on the Quiet Side
cards.subtitle: Bauccio Commons
cards.notes: Use the quieter side for a meal-and-reading break when it is not reserved, and plan ahead if you need a wall outlet for longer work.
cards.short_summary: A designated quieter side of the campus commons that can support study alongside dining.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland identifies the Quiet Side of Bauccio Commons as a study option when it is not otherwise in use.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Use only when not otherwise in use; dining purchases may be required for food.

cards.title: Pause in Holy Cross Lounge
cards.subtitle: Third floor, Franz Hall
cards.notes: Head to the third floor for a quiet reading session; use the available seating and outlets considerately, especially during busy class periods.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor Franz Hall lounge with banquette seating and a quiet atmosphere.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland places Holy Cross Lounge on the third floor of Franz Hall and describes it as quiet and peaceful, with seating and outlets.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located across from the Garaventa Center entrance in Franz Hall.

cards.title: Meet up in St. Mary’s Lounge
cards.subtitle: St. Mary’s Student Center
cards.notes: Choose this lounge for collaborative work or a casual meet-up, and shift to a quieter setting if you need uninterrupted concentration.
cards.short_summary: A lounge in the student center described by the University as an active hangout space.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland describes the St. Mary’s lounge as a college hangout space where activity is commonly taking place.
cards.source_title: Best Places to Study on Campus
cards.access_notes: Located in St. Mary’s Student Center; access may vary with student-center programming.

cards.title: Move between study sessions
cards.subtitle: Beauchamp Recreation & Wellness Center
cards.notes: Bring appropriate workout gear, check current recreation policies, and choose a court, track, climbing, fitness, or equipment activity that fits your plan.
cards.short_summary: A campus recreation facility supporting exercise, climbing, basketball, bike rentals, and more.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland lists basketball, weights, bike rentals, climbing, and other activities at the Beauchamp Recreation and Wellness Center.
cards.access_notes: Recreation access and equipment use are subject to current Recreational Services policies.

cards.title: Join a garden activity at S.L.U.G.
cards.subtitle: Student Led Unity Garden, 6615 N. McKenna Ave.
cards.notes: Watch for registered garden programs, then join hands-on planting or activities with the organizers’ directions and the site’s weather-ready guidance.
cards.short_summary: A named campus garden used for hands-on planting and community activities.
cards.evidence_claim: UP Biology describes the Student Led Unity Garden as the site of a University of Portland hands-on gardening and community event.
cards.access_notes: Event participation may require advance registration and is subject to organizer instructions.

cards.title: Attend Mass or take a reflective pause
cards.subtitle: Chapel of Christ the Teacher
cards.notes: Check Campus Ministry’s current schedule before attending Mass or other programs, and use the space respectfully around services and individual reflection.
cards.short_summary: The University chapel hosts Mass and is central to Campus Ministry programming.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s 2025–26 viewbook states that students may attend Mass in the Chapel of Christ the Teacher and join Campus Ministry programs.
cards.access_notes: Religious services and programs follow Campus Ministry’s current schedule.

cards.title: Look for an exhibit in Buckley
cards.subtitle: First floor, Buckley Center
cards.notes: Check the University calendar for the current exhibition or reception, then visit during its listed access window and follow any gallery instructions.
cards.short_summary: A first-floor Buckley Center gallery used for University exhibition programming.
cards.evidence_claim: University of Portland’s event calendar identifies the Buckley Center Art Gallery on the first floor as a venue for an art exhibit and reception.
cards.source_title: Buckley Center | University of Portland Events Calendar
cards.access_notes: Exhibition availability depends on the University’s current calendar and gallery schedule.
